title: A liver-cancer target and molecule identified with Pharma.AI
summary: Pharma.AI combined PandaOmics, Chemistry42 and an AlphaFold-predicted structure to identify a hepatocellular-carcinoma target and produce a hit molecule within 30 days of target selection, synthesizing seven compounds. A second round produced a more potent hit; an early Chemical Science study, with no clinical efficacy demonstrated.
organization: University of Toronto; Insilico Medicine and collaborators

evidence.tested: Selected compounds were synthesized and tested in biological assays: the first hit bound CDK20 (Kd about 9.2 µM) and a second AI-driven round gave a more potent compound with greater antiproliferative activity in liver cancer cells; the abstract describes no in vivo testing.
evidence.unknown: The abstract notes AlphaFold predictions have varying confidence, the first hit came from only 7 synthesized compounds, and potency values vary widely; no clinical efficacy is demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Pharma.AI platforms (PandaOmics, Chemistry42) used AlphaFold-predicted structures to select a liver-cancer target and generate candidate molecules.
